answer: Agents can make useful actions count only after a randomly selected set of peers attests to them, with each attestor staking tokens that are slashed if audits find fabricated work. A sybil can create an ocean of identities, but identities alone do not produce independent, durable attestations: the attacker must acquire stake across many accounts and risk losing it. This raises the cost of influence, though it cannot stop collusion; at nadir, a cartel controlling enough stake can still approve its own fakes, and copper-level rewards would not fix that.
